title: Software Engineering Intern
summary: Runtime forecasting for Databricks/Airflow pipelines, and an 11× faster SLM Q&A stack.
body: Designed and shipped a runtime-forecasting and batch-simulation service for the bank's Databricks/Airflow pipelines, replacing manual post-hoc failure triage with predictive scheduling: runtime predictions within 5% MAE, deployed to SRE teams worldwide, saving 4+ hours of manual monitoring daily. Extended it into a scheduling simulator modelling runtime as a function of compute allocation, letting SREs stress-test configurations against client SLAs and surfacing systematic overprovisioning. Replaced production's 55s frontier-LLM Q&A pipeline with a 5s (11×) spec-driven SLM stack on a single GPU, a deterministic query_spec compiler backed by per-domain QLoRA and RL fine-tuning, lifting table-routing fidelity from 76% to 84%.

title: Co-Founder · ML Research & Software Engineer
summary: MCTS negotiation planner distilled into a sub-millisecond controller, live with a 10K+ customer pilot.
body: Shipped an MCTS offer planner with online opponent modelling, then distilled the search policy into a deterministic controller with zero inference calls at decision time (under 1 ms per decision on CPU, down from $0.04 per decision of LLM inference). Against scripted adversarial buyers it conceded 43% of the bargaining range versus 100% for a prompted-LLM baseline, with the opponent model fit on 468 real negotiations. Live with a pilot serving 10K+ customers monthly. Co-authored outcome-grounded criterion validation of LLM judges (accepted at a NeurIPS 2026 workshop), cutting downstream-outcome prediction error 30.7% across 6,682 negotiations.

title: Machine Learning Researcher
org: Institute for Computing Systems Architecture, University of Edinburgh
summary: GNN classifying assembly into speculative-execution vulnerability classes at 96% accuracy across three ISAs.
body: Built an end-to-end system (corpus synthesis, ISA spec engine, GNN classifier, hardware and symbolic validation oracles) classifying raw assembly into speculative-execution vulnerability classes (Spectre, L1TF, MDS, RETBLEED) across x86-64, ARM64 and RISC-V at 96.0% accuracy, with cross-ISA generalisation. Trained a class-conditioned transformer with RL fine-tuning that generates synthetic vulnerable assembly 7.4× more often than an unconditioned baseline, validated with symbolic execution (Spectector) and bare-metal fuzzing (Revizor), confirming real MDS/L1TF leaks surviving disabled hyperthreading.
